purpose: Tactile visual expressions rooted in sensory support, bridging organic material and technology. Every generated image must serve a declared sensory role.
principles: Choose a sensory function before choosing an aesthetic.
Compose a continuous tactile surface, field or material terrain. Material qualities alone do not make an isolated abstract object a brand surface.
Individual units may be visible, but they must aggregate into a coherent tactile field; crop and scale should imply continuation beyond the image.
Use light, texture, depth and rhythm intentionally; organic and technological expressions belong to one material vocabulary.
Technology is expressed through precision, repetition, microstructure and light; avoid generic futuristic imagery.
Preserve a quiet reading zone or place content on a separate solid surface.
Offer variation and choice; sensory preferences differ. Do not claim an image universally calms, regulates or treats anyone.
Static imagery does not authorize motion. Motion needs its own contract and static alternative.
Surfaces may be smooth, rough, spiky or mixed. Sensory support does not prescribe softness: choose texture by declared sensory intent and offer variation without assuming universal preferences.
Encourage variety from asset to asset. Glossy, matte, velvet, sanded and other intentional finishes are permitted; do not impose one default material treatment across the brand.

requiredBrief.sensoryIntent: One plain-language sentence describing the intended experience without medical claims.
requiredBrief.placement: Named product, editorial, social or video placement
requiredBrief.material: Specific tactile material and its behavior under light
requiredBrief.detailDistribution: Describe where detail concentrates and where it recedes
requiredBrief.contentZone: Named empty/quiet region, or separate solid content surface
requiredBrief.palette: Named brand anchors with exact hex values
requiredBrief.lighting: Direction, diffusion, highlight and contrast character
requiredBrief.composition: Focal hierarchy, negative space, camera/depth and crop requirements
requiredBrief.responsiveCrops: Required alternate ratios and protected regions
requiredBrief.motion: static by default; separate motion contract if requested
requiredBrief.alternative: Lower-detail or flatter companion when needed
requiredBrief.surfaceConstruction: How the material forms a continuous plane, connected folds, packed bed or coherent terrain rather than an isolated object arrangement.
requiredBrief.unitScaleAndDensity: Size and density of repeated units relative to the frame; explain how the aggregate reads as a surface.
requiredBrief.edgeBehavior: How the material continues beyond the crop; avoid complete object silhouettes posed in empty space.
requiredBrief.surfaceTexture: smooth | rough | spiky | mixed; describe tactile quality, feature scale, density and transitions
requiredBrief.surfaceFinish: Open vocabulary: glossy, matte, velvet, sanded or another intentional finish; describe reflection, grain and light response.

families.name: Soft blush pearl veils
families.intent: Offer a gentle material atmosphere and visual breathing room.
families.material: Soft translucent pearlescent folds; fine tactile grain; not jewelry.
families.detail: Broad folds, diffused light and sparse highlights. Keep the content zone low-detail.
families.prompt: Create a DesignA11y tactile sensory surface for {{placement}}, intended to offer gentle visual breathing room. A continuous edge-to-edge pearlescent material surface with broad organic folds that extend beyond the crop, delicate fine grain, diffused light, restrained depth. Palette: Blush #F4DDE7 and Petal #FAF7F8, subtle Rose #D99AAE; Copper #E8B08F only as a restrained reflected warmth if needed. Keep {{contentZone}} quiet with low local detail and soft tonal variation. Concentrate material definition in {{detailZone}}. Compose for {{aspectRatio}} and protect {{cropSafeRegion}}. Static, refined, editorial, original. No isolated objects, complete sculptural silhouettes, product still lifes, text, logos, interface, jewelry, literal pearls, hard glitter, sharp caustics, busy noise or unrelated objects.

families.name: Glass ribbon
families.intent: Use a controlled material gesture to guide the eye and connect parts of a composition.
families.material: A continuous translucent glass-like folded surface with flowing ribbon-like ridges; not a freestanding ribbon object.
families.detail: One directional flow within a connected material field; close crop implies continuation beyond the image.
families.prompt: Create a DesignA11y tactile sensory surface for {{placement}}, intended to guide the eye through a continuous material flow. Close-cropped translucent glass-like folds and ribbon-like ridges form one connected surface extending beyond every relevant edge, bridging organic movement and technological precision. No standalone ribbon sculpture. Aubergine #442A42 depth, restrained Copper #E8B08F grazing light, subtle Blush #F4DDE7 and Petal #FAF7F8 reflections. Direct the flow through {{detailZone}} while keeping {{contentZone}} quiet. Smooth tonal falloff and controlled highlights. Compose for {{aspectRatio}} and protect {{cropSafeRegion}}. Static, tactile, editorial. No isolated spheres, object arrangements, product still life, text, logos, UI, neon cyberpunk, circuitry, chrome clutter, sharp glare or blown highlights.

families.name: Copper-lit aubergine field
families.intent: Invite optional close looking and sensory curiosity through coherent microstructure.
families.material: Dense but ordered open-corner microgeometry with tactile depth and controlled luminous edges.
families.detail: Texture concentrates below; distant structure softens into quiet Aubergine. Essential text stays separate.
families.prompt: Create a DesignA11y tactile sensory field for {{placement}}, intended for optional close looking and sensory curiosity. A material landscape of tiny precise open L-shaped corner elements arranged as a coherent organic terrain, forming a connected densely repeated surface that continues beyond the crop, not scattered objects or random confetti. Aubergine #442A42 ground, Copper #E8B08F illumination, restrained Petal #FAF7F8 glints and subtle Blush #F4DDE7 reflection. Use grazing light, shallow depth transitions and a clear focal region in {{detailZone}}. Let the upper/distant field recede into quiet Aubergine; keep {{contentZone}} separate or genuinely low-detail. Compose for {{aspectRatio}} and {{cropSafeRegion}}. Static image only. No text, logos, complete brand symbols, UI, circuitry, server racks, sci-fi grids, neon cyan, glitter explosions, high-frequency interference, visual flicker or unrelated objects.

families.name: Magnetic-sphere surface
families.intent: Invite tactile curiosity through densely packed repetition and small-scale material detail.
families.material: Many small magnetic-bead-like spheres forming a dense connected bed or gently folded terrain.
families.detail: Speks-like tactile aggregation is a structural reference; use original unbranded imagery. No single dominant sphere. Units meet and collectively read as a surface.
families.prompt: Create an original DesignA11y tactile sensory surface for {{placement}}, intended for optional close looking. A macro view of hundreds of small, densely packed magnetic-bead-like spheres forms one coherent continuous material bed with subtle folds and shallow terrain. Think of the tactile aggregation of a magnetic-sphere fidget, not a product shot or branded replica. Individual beads remain small relative to the frame; no single hero sphere, no handful of floating balls. The packed material continues beyond the crop. Aubergine #442A42 shaded depth, restrained Copper #E8B08F and Rose #D99AAE reflections, soft Petal #FAF7F8 highlights. Controlled grazing light reveals contact and fine texture without sharp glare. Concentrate detail in {{detailZone}}, preserve quiet {{contentZone}}, compose for {{aspectRatio}} with {{cropSafeRegion}} protected. Static and editorial. No logos, text, packaging, isolated sculptures, freestanding glass ribbons, disconnected objects, glitter bursts or high-frequency interference.

steps: Validate required brief fields; return missing fields before generation.
Validate surface construction: reject isolated objects even if their materials and palette fit. For repeated units, require enough small connected units to read as a continuous field.
Choose the closest family by sensory role and intended placement.
Expand placeholders using the brief; unresolved placeholders are an error.
Generate one role-specific image and retain the resolved prompt, model/version/settings when available, date and source references.
Review composition at output size and all required crops; reject outputs that lose quiet zones, hierarchy or motif integrity.
Check text contrast on the final composite or use a solid content surface; never infer contrast from palette alone.
Record human review, alternative-text decision, limitations and export variants.
rejectIf: Brand content replaced by unrelated travel/lifestyle narrative
Motion inferred from a still-image brief
Object-led still life or standalone abstract sculpture instead of a surface
One dominant sphere or a few floating spheres when the intended subject is a bead surface
Material does not continue beyond the crop and lacks coherent aggregation

accessibility.sensoryClaims: Intent, not proven effect. No universal comfort or therapeutic claims.
accessibility.decorative: Empty alt in HTML when purely decorative.
accessibility.color: Do not communicate essential meaning through color alone.
accessibility.motion: Separate reduced-motion and playback requirements; static remains default.
accessibility.evidence: Generation prompts are not accessibility certification.

reject: Isolated hero sphere or small still-life grouping
Floating ribbon presented as a standalone sculpture
Decorative arrangement of glass, pearl and copper objects
Correct materials without a coherent surface construction

negativeReference.observation: Hero contains a single pearlescent sphere, glass ribbon and copper object; lower field repeats a large spherical object. Materials are compatible, but object-led composition is rejected.
negativeReference.scope: Image composition only; do not adopt the screenshot's old copy, eyebrow or layout.

textureGuidance.selection: Choose texture independently from sensory role, material, palette and organic/technology balance. Smooth is not the only acceptable sensory expression; rough or spiky is not automatically excessive.
control: Specify feature scale, spacing, density, sharpness and highlight behavior.
Keep repeated texture coherent as a continuous surface or terrain.
Review visual intensity at final size; dense sharp detail can compete with reading zones.
Provide a quieter or lower-detail companion where needed; do not claim any texture is universally calming or uncomfortable.
textureGuidance.promptClause: Surface texture: {{surfaceTexture}}. Describe {{textureScale}}, {{textureDensity}} and {{textureTransitions}} explicitly. Maintain a coherent continuous material field; preserve {{contentZone}} and control highlights for the intended sensory intensity.

finishGuidance.distinction: Texture describes surface structure; finish describes material and light response. Combine intentionally, for example rough matte, smooth glossy, spiky velvet-like or finely sanded.
finishGuidance.assetVariety: Variety is encouraged from asset to asset. Maintain coherence through sensory purpose, surface construction, brand palette and composition rather than identical texture or finish.
finishGuidance.promptClause: Finish: {{surfaceFinish}}. Specify its reflection, grain and light response. Choose a treatment appropriate to this asset; do not repeat a previous asset's finish by default.
